The Season of Censorship we're currently witnessing in gaming is a sad reminder that while SJWs are tiny fringe minority (which most of the gaming community is sick off, just witness the response to PlayAsia calling them out), they're still loud enough to negatively impact our community. I think part of the problem is that every time SJWs attack individual games, the people opposing them merely try to debunk their specific accusations, when the accusations the SJWs put out there ("this game is Sexist/Racist/Culturally Insensitive/Sexualizing Under Aged Characters") are themselves currently perceived as so damaging that whenever they come up, many companies simply want them issue to go away and cave immediately. I believe the more effective response in the long run is undermining the very Premises on which the SJW Censorship campaigns are based, while attacking the concept of Censorship itself - the end goal being that devs and companies would fear accusations of Censorship more than they'd fear any accusation SJWs throw at them.

Premises that need to be challenged

Sexist games/content should be Censored or Banned: Whenever SJWs attack a particular game as sexist, I see lots of GG people rush in to defend said game and explain why it's not in fact, sexist. Common arguments are that SJWs misrepresent the game (in fact, they pretty much always do), that what SJWs call "Objectification" is actually empowering, and that said game has lots of female fans. All that is fine as far as it goes, but it means that the next time SJWs smear a game as sexist, we have to go through the same song and dance all over again.

But what if we said "the game might be sexist, so what?" We already accept games that are very violent and disturbing, because we're sane people able to separate reality from fiction - why can't we do the same with sexist games? Even if you had a RapeTown game where all you did was go around raping women, no actual people would be harmed, nor is there reason to think any gamer would end up concluding that raping people in real life is a good idea.

Of course, a RapeTown game is just an extreme example, but the general idea that Something Needs To Be Done about sexist games is a real problem. It gives SJWs ammo against any game that features so much as a scantily clad female character, or a scene where a female character is subjected to the kind of violence that male characters are victims of all the time. Instead of playing Defense, attack the very concept of video game sexism being harmful and dangerous, and instead advocate that gamers be treated like adults able to decide for themselves what kind of content is and is not acceptable. Creative freedom is about being free to explore all sorts of issues and scenarios - that shouldn't be limited by cries of "sexism" or "misogyny".

Racist/Culturally Insensitive games/content should be Censored or Banned: SJWs also throw these labels around willy-nilly (including at games that are simply being historically accurate), but the power of the accusation is why they do it - they know how much companies operating in the West fear the accusation of Racism, and so they keep clubbing people and games with it.

Again, what happened to games being recognized as fiction? It didn't use to be that people freaked out over ethnic stereotypes - just look at Punch Out!, a beloved, iconic game series that's composed of almost nothing but ethnic stereotypes. Seems that in the past, we recognized that funny stereotypes are not the same as Stormfront propaganda, and even when caricatures actually do slide into racist territory it's hardly this huge cultural crisis. How about we start openly advocating the position that the creative freedom of creators being stifled is a greater evil than any "problematic" element in a work of fiction?

Homophobic/Fatphobic/Transphobic/Otherkinphobic etc games/content should be Censored or Banned: I think you've gotten a good idea of where I'm going with this - don't settle with saying that the games attacked by SJWs aren't offensive, straight up fight for the right of games to be offensive!

Games/content sexualizing under aged characters should be Censored or Banned: I don't really see this line of SJW attack be challenged much either on principles OR the merits of individual games they attack, so here are my suggestions for both.

Let's start with the obvious point here: It's ridiculous to obsess about Age of CONSENT when it comes to FICTIONAL characters who aren't going to be able to consent to matter how old you make them, because their actions (just like their age and everything else about them) is controlled by someone else, namely the creator. Don't forget that SJWs also go after characters that LOOK under age, but are canonically 100s of years old, so the SJWs themselves don't even care about fictional AoC, it's just an excuse. Thing is, they've completely misunderstood why we have AoC laws and laws against child porn in the first place - it's about preventing actual harm befalling actual children, not simply combating stuff we find "icky". No ACTUAL harm is caused by skimpily dressed fictional 15 year olds appearing in some Japanese games.

Moreover, the SJW definition of "sexualized" is ridiculous: By their standards, pretty much every single girl under 18 on the beach is sexualized. It's almost like THEY are the kind of sick people who constantly sexualize kids...which nicely ties into the case of srhbutts. Simply put, we now know he's not just an admitted pedophile, but that he distributed actual child porn (there's no "edgelord" exception to the law against CP, so even if he wasn't lying about that, it wouldn't matter). And despite all this, the vast majority of SJWs still defend and even outright support him. The fact that SJWs keep throwing around false accusations of pedophilia, while rushing to defend an ACTUAL pedophile, just tells me that they're using this argument to further the cause of Censorship, not actually protect kids.

My main point is that until we mobilize strong support for The Right To Be Offense we're just gonna be playing whack-a-mole and be on the Defensive (likewise with game devs).
